summary: Because Ansible resources model desired state, you should not write tests that services are started or packages installed; instead declare the state and Ansible will fail if it cannot achieve it.
questions: Should I write tests to check a service is running after Ansible starts it?
How do I make sure a service is started and enabled?
What should I test in an Ansible deployment?

answer_card.title: Declare state instead of testing it
answer_card.answer_md:
Ansible modules enforce desired state, so you don't need tests that packages are installed or services are started. Just declare it:

```yaml
- ansible.builtin.service:
    name: foo
    state: started
    enabled: true
```

If the service fails to start, Ansible reports a failure. Whether the service actually works functionally is a separate check.
